grammar.title: Future Continuous and Future Perfect
grammar.explanation:
The **future continuous** (**will be** + -ing) describes an action in progress at a future time. For example, this time tomorrow you **will be shopping** for a jacket.

The **future perfect** (**will have** + past participle) describes an action finished before a future time. By Friday, you **will have paid** the full amount.

Use **will have been** + -ing (the **future perfect continuous**) to say how long something will have continued. By June, she **will have been working** here for five years.

Use the future perfect with **by** and **by the time** for completion. After **by the time**, **when**, **before** and **until**, use a **present** tense, not **will**.
examples: *This time next week, we**'ll be lying** on a beach.* (in progress)
*I**'ll be waiting** for you at the station at 6.* (in progress)
*By the time we get there, the film **will have started**.* (completed before)
*I**'ll have finished** this book by Friday.* (by + time)
*Next month, I**'ll have been learning** English for three years.* (duration)
*By the time she retires, she**'ll have taught** thousands of students.* (total by a future time)

practice.q: Rewrite with the future continuous: Tomorrow at 10, I shop for a jacket.
practice.a: Tomorrow at 10, I'll be shopping for a jacket.

practice.q: Rewrite with the future perfect: By Friday, I pay the full amount.
practice.a: By Friday, I'll have paid the full amount.

practice.q: Rewrite with the future perfect: By next year, we consolidate our debts.
practice.a: By next year, we'll have consolidated our debts.

practice.q: Correct the mistake: By the time you will arrive, we'll have eaten.
practice.a: By the time you arrive, we'll have eaten.
